hero.headline: Extreme heat threatens July 4th celebrations across US
hero.body:
A severe heat wave is disrupting July 4th celebrations across the United States as the country marks its 250th birthday. The extreme temperatures have forced changes to outdoor events and raised public safety concerns in multiple cities.

Washington DC has altered its July Fourth weekend event plans in response to the oppressive conditions. The heat dome has trapped approximately 260 million people under scorching temperatures that are expected to last through the holiday. Major metropolitan areas including New York City, Philadelphia, Boston, and Washington DC are experiencing the most intense effects.

The Mid-Atlantic region has reached peak heat levels, with numerous temperature records falling across the eastern United States. Maryland faces extreme heat through July 4th, with forecasters warning of an increased risk of storms as the weather system continues. The combination of record-breaking temperatures and high humidity has created dangerous conditions for outdoor gatherings traditionally held during the Independence Day holiday.

Authorities are urging residents to take precautions during outdoor activities and to monitor vulnerable populations. The heat wave's timing coincides with one of the busiest travel and celebration periods of the year, when millions of Americans typically gather for parades, barbecues, and fireworks displays. Event organizers across affected regions have been forced to reassess safety protocols and make last-minute adjustments to scheduled activities.

The extreme weather pattern represents a significant disruption to the milestone anniversary celebrations. Public health officials continue to monitor the situation as the heat dome shows little sign of weakening through the holiday weekend.

cards.headline: Russian Strikes Kill 21 in Kyiv as Ukraine Hits Deeper Into Russian Territory
cards.body:
At least 21 people were killed in Russian attacks on Kyiv, according to local authorities in the Ukrainian capital. The strikes represent one of the most significant assaults on the city in recent months, with Russian forces deploying a large number of weapons across a wide area.

The deadly bombardment came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had previously warned that Moscow was preparing a massive strike on the city. The attack appears to have fulfilled those warnings, following a pattern of Russian military operations targeting civilian infrastructure and population centers in Ukraine's major cities.

The escalation reflects intensifying military operations on both sides of the conflict. Ukrainian forces have demonstrated an increased capacity to strike military and infrastructure targets deep into Russian territory, disrupting Russian supply lines and military capabilities. These long-range operations, however, have prompted increasingly severe Russian responses against Ukrainian population centers.

On Saturday, Russian strikes in the Dnipropetrovsk region of central-eastern Ukraine and the northern Sumy region killed two people. The same day, Ukrainian attacks on the Russian border regions of Volgograd and Belgorod resulted in three deaths, according to regional authorities. A Ukrainian drone strike in Russia's Bryansk region killed two people in a vehicle near the border, according to the region's acting governor Yegor Kovalchuk. Russia's defense ministry reported that 124 Ukrainian drones were downed over Russian regions during a 12-hour period.

A massive Ukrainian drone strike also hit the Krasnodar region in southern Russia, killing one person and wounding another. The attack caused a fire at an oil refinery and damaged several houses with falling debris, according to regional governor Veniamin Kondratyev. A power line and gas pipe were also damaged in the strike.

In southeastern Ukraine, more than 40 drone strikes and artillery attacks on the town of Nikopol, which lies opposite the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killed one person and injured another, according to the regional governor of Dnipropetrovsk.

The back-and-forth strikes highlight the ongoing intensity of the conflict, with neither side showing signs of backing down from military operations. The targeting of Kyiv, Ukraine's largest city and political center, carries both strategic and symbolic weight for Russia. Meanwhile, Ukraine's strikes into Russian territory represent a significant shift in the operational dynamics of the war. The civilian casualties on both sides underscore the human cost as the conflict continues with no immediate resolution in sight.

cards.headline: Iran warns of response if US breaches interim peace deal
cards.teaser: Tehran's Parliament Speaker says Iran will act if the United States and Israel fail to meet their commitments under the agreement.
cards.body:
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has warned that Iran will respond if the United States and Israel violate terms of an interim peace deal between the countries. The warning comes as Tehran prepares for the funeral of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Ghalibaf stated that Iran demands full implementation of agreements reached with the United States, signaling Tehran's intent to hold Washington accountable for its commitments. He did not specify what form a potential Iranian response might take.

cards.headline: Foreign Leaders Gather in Iran for Khamenei Funeral Ceremonies
cards.teaser: China, Russia, Pakistan and other nations send dignitaries to pay respects as Iran begins days of ceremonies for its deceased supreme leader.
cards.body:
Foreign dignitaries from China, Russia, Pakistan and other nations arrived in Iran on Friday to pay respects to Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Khamenei was killed in a US-Israeli attack in February. His body lay in state at Tehran's Grand Mosalla ahead of the multi-day funeral ceremony.

The six-day funeral begins Saturday in Tehran and concludes Thursday with Khamenei's burial in Mashhad. Iranian officials describe the ceremony as intended to demonstrate national power and resilience. At the request of Iraqi politicians, Khamenei's body will also be carried through Shia cities in Iraq, including Karbala.

cards.headline: Gas Shortages Hit Russia as Long Lines Form at Pumps
cards.teaser: Russians expressed frustration at fuel shortages, with one asking if the country had returned to Soviet-era conditions.
cards.body:
Long lines formed at gas stations across Russia as fuel shortages disrupted what many Russians had considered normal life during wartime. The shortages shattered the appearance of stability that had persisted despite ongoing military operations.

One Russian, stunned and frustrated by the waits at the pumps, asked whether the country had returned to Soviet Union conditions. The fuel shortages represent a visible sign of economic strain that had previously been less apparent to ordinary Russians in their daily lives.

cards.headline: France Reports Over 2,000 Heat Deaths as Europe Braces for More Extreme Weather
cards.teaser: France recorded 2,025 excess deaths at the peak of a heatwave, with forecasters warning of further extreme temperatures across the continent.
cards.body:
France recorded 2,025 excess deaths during a recent heatwave, according to figures released Friday. The deaths underscore the serious health threat posed by extreme temperatures sweeping across Europe.

Last week's heatwave shattered temperature records across the continent. The UK hit a provisional peak of 37.7°C in Norfolk on June 27, breaking the previous June record by an exceptional 2.1°C. Germany reached an all-time high of 41.7°C. Forecasters warn that further extreme weather is expected in the coming days, with ongoing risks to vulnerable populations including the elderly and those with pre-existing health conditions.

cards.headline: NASA launches mission to rescue Swift space telescope before it burns up in atmosphere
cards.body:
NASA launched a rescue mission to save the Swift space telescope, which has been falling back toward Earth and faces destruction if it reenters the atmosphere. A NASA-funded robot blasted off to intercept the telescope in mid-orbit and boost it back to a safe altitude.

The Swift telescope, which has been operating in space for years, has been gradually losing altitude due to atmospheric drag. Without intervention, the spacecraft would eventually burn up during reentry. The rescue mission represents an attempt to extend the operational life of the valuable scientific instrument.

The mission involves a robotic spacecraft that will rendezvous with Swift in orbit. Once the two spacecraft meet, the rescue vehicle will use its propulsion system to push Swift back into a higher, more stable orbit. This maneuver aims to prevent the telescope from succumbing to the increasing atmospheric resistance that has been pulling it downward.

The Swift observatory has provided crucial data for astronomical research during its time in space. Saving the telescope would allow scientists to continue using its instruments for studying cosmic phenomena. The rescue effort demonstrates NASA's commitment to preserving functioning space assets that still have scientific value.

Reports indicated that a last-minute technical problem caused a brief delay before the rescue mission successfully launched. The spacecraft is now on its way to attempt the complex orbital rendezvous and rescue operation that will determine whether Swift can continue its scientific mission or will be lost to atmospheric reentry.

cards.headline: Interpol Names Ukrainian Woman as Main Suspect in Monaco Bombing
cards.teaser: Monaco prosecutors say the suspect identified by international police is no longer in the principality following the bomb attack.
cards.body:
Interpol has issued a red notice for Anastasiia Berezovska, 39, a Ukrainian woman identified as the main suspect in a bomb attack in Monaco. According to authorities, the suspect disguised herself as a man and is believed to be living in Germany. She is described as German-speaking with dark hair and a distinctive tattoo of possibly a snake on her right arm.

The parcel bomb seriously injured Vadym Iermolaiev, a Ukraine-born business tycoon, along with two family members. Prosecutors confirm the suspect is no longer in Monaco, and Interpol's involvement reflects the international scope of the investigation.

cards.headline: Tibetan Activist Dies After Self-Immolation Outside United Nations
cards.teaser: A 52-year-old Queens resident set himself on fire in protest against Chinese policies he said were destroying the Tibetan people.
cards.body:
Lobga Rangzen, a 52-year-old Tibetan activist and Queens resident, died after setting himself on fire outside the United Nations in New York. Rangzen said Beijing's policies were destroying the Tibetan people, according to statements he made before the act.

The self-immolation represents one of the most extreme forms of political protest, a tactic that has been used by Tibetan activists in the past to draw attention to Chinese government actions in Tibet. The incident took place at the international organization's headquarters, a symbolic location chosen to maximize visibility of the protest.

cards.headline: At Least 32 Killed in Pakistan Bus Crash
cards.teaser: An overcrowded bus plunged into a ravine in the Dana Sar mountain range while traveling from Quetta to Peshawar.
cards.body:
At least 32 people died when an overcrowded bus crashed in Pakistan's Dana Sar mountain range on Friday. The vehicle was traveling from Quetta to Peshawar when the accident occurred, with the bus plunging into a ravine.

The crash underscores persistent safety challenges on Pakistan's mountain roads, where overcrowded buses regularly traverse treacherous terrain. Overcrowding on passenger vehicles is a recurring factor that increases the severity of accidents in these regions.

cards.headline: USAID shutdown reaches one-year mark
cards.teaser: A former administrator reflects on the year since the US Agency for International Development closed operations.
cards.body:
The former head of USAID has spoken about the year since the agency's shutdown, expressing both grief over its closure and hope for the future of US foreign aid. The administrator reflected on the agency's closure and the new direction American foreign assistance has taken.

The comments come as the shutdown reaches its one-year anniversary. USAID had served as the primary US government agency responsible for administering civilian foreign aid and development assistance before its operations ended.

cards.headline: Monaco prosecutor names suspect in bomb attack
cards.teaser: Interpol has identified a Ukrainian woman as the main suspect in a bombing in Monaco.
cards.body:
Monaco's prosecutor's office announced that a Ukrainian woman has been named by Interpol as the primary suspect in a bomb attack that occurred in the principality. The prosecutor's office stated that the suspect is no longer in Monaco.

The investigation continues as authorities work to locate the woman identified in the international alert. Interpol's involvement indicates the cross-border nature of the search for the suspect.

cards.headline: Man sentenced for 2009 killing in Crete
cards.teaser: A Greek man received a 10-year sentence for killing a Scottish woman whose body was found off the coast of Crete.
cards.body:
A Greek court has found a man guilty of murdering Jean Hanlon from Dumfries. He has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for the killing. Hanlon's body was discovered in the waters off Crete in 2009.

The case went unsolved for nearly two decades before the conviction was reached, bringing closure to the long-running investigation into her death on the Greek island.

cards.headline: Burnham signals limited tax flexibility
cards.teaser: The likely next British prime minister says he will maintain Labour's pledge not to raise major taxes.
cards.body:
Andy Burnham has signaled some flexibility on tax policy while reaffirming Labour's core commitments. The likely next prime minister said he will maintain the party's pledges not to raise VAT, income tax, or national insurance.

His comments suggest an approach that allows room for movement on taxation within the boundaries of these key promises.

cards.headline: Police object to late pub hours decision for England match
cards.teaser: Law enforcement officials say the late announcement extending pub hours will require pulling officers from other duties.
cards.body:
The National Police Chiefs' Council has criticized the timing of a decision to extend pub opening hours to 05:00 on Monday for an England match against Mexico. The force said the late announcement creates operational challenges, as it requires reassigning officers from other duties to manage public safety during the extended drinking period.

The council indicated that earlier notice would have enabled better resource planning. The match is scheduled to kick off at 1am on Monday, leading to calls for flexible working arrangements across employers.

cards.headline: Employers urged to show flexibility after 1am England match
cards.teaser: Businesses are being encouraged to allow staff flexible work arrangements following a late-night World Cup game.
cards.body:
Employers are being urged to use "common sense" in allowing staff to work flexibly after England's 1am World Cup match against Mexico. Some companies have already announced adjusted start times, with at least one employer telling staff they can begin work at 11am.

The late kickoff has also prompted wider discussions about accommodations across different sectors. Police have criticized the timing of the decision to extend pub opening hours to 05:00 on Monday, saying the late announcement means officers will be diverted from other duties.

hero.headline: Ford reaches quality milestone as CEO pushes for flawless vehicle launches
hero.body:
Ford Motor Company has achieved a significant quality improvement, placing it as the top mass-market brand in the 2026 J.D. Power U.S. Initial Quality Study. The automaker's CEO is now targeting flawless launches for new vehicles as the company builds on its turnaround from previous quality issues.

The J.D. Power study measures problems reported by vehicle owners during the first 90 days of ownership. Ford's achievement marks a reversal from years of quality concerns that had affected the company's reputation and customer satisfaction scores. The ranking places Ford ahead of other mainstream manufacturers in the mass-market category.

Lexus, which had long held the top position for initial quality across all brands, was surpassed in the 2026 study. Genesis climbed to second place overall in the rankings, demonstrating strong quality performance among luxury brands. The shifts in rankings reflect broader changes in manufacturing quality across the automotive industry.

Ford's quality improvements come as the company invests heavily in new vehicle development and manufacturing processes. The CEO's emphasis on flawless launches indicates a strategic priority on getting products right from the start, rather than addressing problems after vehicles reach customers. This approach aims to reduce warranty costs and build customer loyalty in a competitive market.

The quality milestone represents a significant achievement for Ford as it transitions toward electric vehicles and new technology platforms. Maintaining quality during periods of technological change has proven difficult for many automakers, making Ford's performance particularly notable as the industry undergoes its largest transformation in decades.

cards.headline: Burnham says limited room for movement on tax policy
cards.teaser: The likely next prime minister says he will stick to Labour's pledges not to raise value-added tax, income tax, or national insurance.
cards.body:
Burnham has signalled some flexibility on tax policy, though he remains committed to Labour's key fiscal commitments. The likely next Prime Minister has pledged to maintain the party's promises not to raise VAT, income tax, or national insurance rates.

These three tax pledges form the cornerstone of Labour's fiscal campaign platform and significantly constrain the party's options for raising additional revenue if it enters government.

cards.headline: Employers urged to allow flexible work for England's late-night match
cards.teaser: Bosses are being encouraged to use common sense in letting staff work flexibly after England's 1am match.
cards.body:
Employers are being urged to use "common sense" in allowing staff to work flexibly around England's 1am match. Some companies have already announced they will let employees start work at 11am the following day.

The unusual timing has created challenges beyond the workplace. Police have criticised the late announcement to extend pub opening hours until 05:00 on Monday, saying the decision diverts officers from other duties.

cards.headline: Former John Lewis boss launches workplace sickness taskforce
cards.teaser: More than 250 of the UK's biggest employers have signed up to a taskforce aimed at tackling workplace sickness to unlock economic growth.
cards.body:
A former John Lewis chief executive has launched a 'Get Britain Working' taskforce focused on addressing workplace sickness and absenteeism. The initiative has attracted support from more than 250 major UK employers.

The taskforce aims to reduce employee sickness levels as a means of boosting economic productivity and growth. Workplace absence has become a significant concern for UK businesses, with health-related absences affecting output and competitiveness across multiple sectors.

cards.headline: Study links hot stock markets to major wealth destruction
cards.teaser: Investor enthusiasm in the hottest stock markets culminated in some of the worst cases of wealth destruction over the past century.
cards.body:
A century-long study reveals that stock markets attracting the most investor enthusiasm have historically delivered the largest subsequent losses. Researchers analyzed market performance across multiple speculative periods and found a consistent pattern: when investor optimism drives valuations to unsustainable levels, significant wealth destruction follows.

This relationship between extreme enthusiasm and eventual losses has repeated across different eras and market cycles, suggesting it represents a fundamental market dynamic rather than an isolated occurrence.

cards.headline: Millions may have eaten goat instead of lamb kebabs
cards.teaser: Food testing suggests millions of people likely consumed kebabs marketed as lamb that actually contained goat, skin, and fat.
cards.body:
Testing has revealed that many kebabs sold as lamb contained goat meat, along with skin and fat, affecting potentially millions of consumers. The products were found to contain less than 10 percent sheep meat despite being marketed as lamb.

The findings raise questions about food labeling accuracy and supply chain oversight in the kebab industry. Consumers who believed they were purchasing lamb products received a substantially different meat product, with implications for both religious dietary requirements and consumer protection.

cards.headline: Shipping choke points differ despite fee collection similarities
cards.teaser: The Strait of Malacca may offer a model for fee collection at the Strait of Hormuz, but the waterways have vast differences.
cards.body:
Analysis suggests the Strait of Malacca could provide a blueprint for how Oman and Iran might collect fees in the Strait of Hormuz. However, experts note the two global shipping choke points differ substantially in their characteristics and strategic importance.

The Strait of Malacca has established precedents for fee collection and maritime governance that could inform discussions about the Strait of Hormuz. The vast differences between the waterways include geographic features, traffic patterns, and geopolitical contexts that complicate direct comparisons.

cards.headline: Scientists build synthetic cell capable of feeding, growing and reproducing
cards.teaser: Researchers claim to have created a basic component of life from scratch in a step toward artificial life.
cards.body:
Scientists announced they have built a synthetic cell that can perform the fundamental functions of life. The manmade cell feeds, grows and reproduces, marking what researchers call a milestone in biological engineering.

The achievement represents progress toward creating lab-made life. The synthetic cell possesses a complete life cycle, which could open new possibilities for biological engineering applications. The development has raised concerns about the implications of creating artificial life forms from scratch.

cards.headline: European politician investigating spyware hacked with Pegasus software
cards.teaser: A government customer of NSO Group used Pegasus spyware to hack a politician serving on an EU committee investigating the spyware industry.
cards.body:
Stelios Kouloglou, a Greek member of the European Parliament, had his phone compromised with Pegasus spyware while serving on an EU committee investigating spyware abuses. Researchers at the Citizen Lab at the University of Toronto discovered the repeated attacks against his device occurred after he joined the parliamentary committee.

The hacking campaign bore similarities to previous attacks against exiled Russian and Belarusian journalists in Europe, though researchers could not definitively attribute the attacks to a specific government operator of the NSO Group software.

cards.headline: Sony begins repurposing PlayStation disc factory ahead of physical media phase-out
cards.teaser: Sony has started converting its only PlayStation disc manufacturing facility as the company prepares to end physical disc production.
cards.body:
Sony's Thalgau plant in Austria is being repurposed as the company winds down physical disc production for PlayStation. The facility currently produces 600,000 discs daily, with half dedicated to PlayStation games, according to Sony DADC president Dietmar Tanzer.

The shift aligns with Sony's previously announced plan to end physical disc production for new PlayStation games in January 2028, marking a significant transition away from physical media in console gaming.

cards.headline: Solar storms could bring northern lights to multiple states over July 4 weekend
cards.teaser: The sun fired off 10 solar flares in 24 hours, with multiple Earth-bound coronal mass ejections raising aurora viewing hopes.
cards.body:
The sun unleashed 10 solar flares within 24 hours, sending waves of charged particles toward Earth. This solar activity has prompted forecasters to issue a strong northern lights forecast for the Fourth of July weekend.

The aurora could be visible across nine U.S. states, offering sky watchers in areas that rarely experience the phenomenon a chance to see the northern lights. The timing coincides with the holiday weekend when many people will be outdoors.

cards.headline: Apple seeks dismissal of lawsuit over YouTube AI training data
cards.teaser: Apple responded to a lawsuit filed by three YouTube channels, asking a court to dismiss the case under DMCA protections.
cards.body:
Apple filed a response to a lawsuit brought by three YouTube channels over allegations related to AI training data. The company is seeking dismissal of the case, arguing that it should be thrown out under provisions of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act.

The lawsuit involves claims about how YouTube content was used in AI training. Apple contends the case fails to meet legal standards under the DMCA. The tech company submitted its formal response asking the court to dismiss the complaint brought by the YouTube content creators.

cards.headline: France records 2,025 excess deaths during peak of heatwave
cards.teaser: French authorities tallied more than 2,000 excess deaths at the height of a heatwave as forecasters warn of more extreme temperatures.
cards.body:
France recorded 2,025 excess deaths at the peak of a recent heatwave that swept across the country. The death toll reflects the severe impact of extreme heat on public health during the hottest days of the weather event.

Forecasters are warning that Europe should brace for additional extreme temperatures in the coming days. The continent faces further dangerous heat conditions after the deadly heatwave that hit France. Weather services have issued alerts about ongoing extreme weather risks across multiple European countries.

hero.headline: Portugal advances to World Cup knockout stage with last-minute win over Croatia
hero.body:
Portugal secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Croatia in their final group stage match, advancing to the Round of 16 and eliminating the Croatian side from the tournament. The decisive moment came in stoppage time when Gonçalo Ramos headed in a goal, sending Portugal through to face Spain in the knockout rounds.

Cristiano Ronaldo opened the scoring from the penalty spot earlier in the match, but the 41-year-old veteran was substituted before the dramatic conclusion. Ronaldo watched from the bench as his team secured the win that ensured their progression.

Croatia mounted a comeback during the match to equalize, setting up a tense finish. The team appeared destined for extra time when they scored late, but video review ruled the goal offside, denying them a chance to extend the contest. The VAR decision proved pivotal, allowing Portugal to claim the three points and knockout stage berth.

The loss marked the end of what was likely Luka Modrić's final World Cup campaign. The 40-year-old midfielder has been central to Croatia's national team for more than a decade, helping lead them to the 2018 final and a third-place finish in 2022. His departure from the tournament represents a significant moment in Croatian football history.

Portugal's victory showcased the squad's depth beyond their established star. Despite Ronaldo's substitution, the team found a way to secure the crucial result through Ramos and other players. The win demonstrated that Portugal possesses viable options across their roster for the knockout stages ahead.

The Iberian neighbors' Round of 16 matchup between Portugal and Spain promises to be one of the tournament's marquee fixtures. The two nations have a long history of competitive matches, and their meeting sets up what many expect to be an entertaining encounter.

Questions linger about whether Ronaldo will retain his starting position going forward. Manager Roberto Martínez decided to bring the forward off the bench against Croatia, a tactical choice that may continue into future matches. The decision suggests the coaching staff is managing Ronaldo's minutes as the tournament progresses.

The final moments of the Portugal-Croatia match encapsulated the intensity of group stage qualification football. Portugal's counterattack caught Croatia vulnerable while they pushed for a late equalizer, leaving them exposed defensively. Ramos capitalized on that opportunity to send his team through.

The dramatic finish underscored how tournament football can turn on single moments. Croatia's disallowed goal illustrated how technology now plays an integral role in World Cup outcomes, with VAR determining which teams advance and which go home.

cards.headline: Lewis Hamilton leads practice session at British Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton posted the fastest time in practice ahead of sprint qualifying at Silverstone.
cards.body:
Lewis Hamilton topped the timesheets in the practice session at the British Grand Prix on Friday. The Ferrari driver set the pace ahead of sprint qualifying, which takes place later that day at Silverstone.

Hamilton's performance suggests Ferrari could be competitive at the historic British circuit as preparations continue for the weekend's racing action.

cards.headline: 76ers enter pursuit of LeBron James after acquiring Jaylen Brown
cards.teaser: Philadelphia has begun pitching LeBron James one day after completing a trade for Jaylen Brown.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have joined the competition for LeBron James, making their pitch to the free agent just one day after acquiring Jaylen Brown in a trade with the Boston Celtics. The move pairs James with Brown and Joel Embiid, potentially creating one of the NBA's strongest rosters.

In the deal that brought Brown to Philadelphia, the Celtics received Paul George along with two first-round picks and two second-round picks. Brown, who won 2024 NBA Finals MVP, had expressed unhappiness with the Celtics before the trade.

cards.headline: Billy Donovan joins Spurs as lead assistant coach
cards.teaser: The former NBA head coach agreed to become the top assistant for San Antonio and head coach Mitch Johnson.
cards.body: Billy Donovan has agreed to join the San Antonio Spurs as lead assistant coach under head coach Mitch Johnson, according to sources. The move marks Donovan's return to the NBA sideline in a coaching capacity following his previous role as a head coach.

cards.headline: Croatia denied equalizer after VAR offside review in World Cup loss
cards.teaser: Video review ruled an offside violation in the buildup to what would have been a game-tying goal for Croatia against Portugal.
cards.body:
Croatia appeared poised to force extra time against Portugal in their World Cup match, but a video assistant referee review determined an offside violation had occurred during the play leading to the goal. The VAR decision resulted in the disallowance of Croatia's equalizer, preserving Portugal's lead in the match.

The controversial call ultimately proved decisive in the outcome of the game.

cards.headline: Julián Quiñones emerges as key player for Mexico ahead of England match
cards.teaser: The forward's unconventional path to the Mexican national team has him positioned as a potential threat in Monday's World Cup matchup.
cards.body:
Julián Quiñones has taken an unconventional route to becoming a crucial player for Mexico at the World Cup. His rise through the ranks differs from the typical path followed by Mexican internationals, yet he has established himself as a scoring threat for the team.

Mexico will rely on Quiñones when they face England on Monday morning in the knockout rounds. His emergence in attack provides the team with additional offensive options as they prepare for one of their most significant tournament matches.

cards.headline: NBA executives weigh in on Jaylen Brown trade and free agency spending
cards.teaser: League insiders discuss the blockbuster Brown deal, major contracts for centers, and an unexpected salary cap development.
cards.body:
The Boston Celtics traded 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in a major offseason blockbuster. Boston received All-Star Paul George along with two first-round picks and two second-round picks in the deal. Brown had expressed unhappiness with his treatment by the Celtics in the weeks leading up to the trade.

As the league entered its second week of free agency, ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported on executive perspectives regarding the Brown trade, the substantial spending on centers across the league, and a significant salary cap development affecting multiple teams.

hero.headline: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Begin Multi-Day Wedding Celebration
hero.body:
Pop star Taylor Swift and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce have begun a multi-day wedding celebration at Madison Square Garden in New York, with preparations underway for what organizers describe as a large-scale event.

According to a permit filed with New York City's permitting office, a "pre-party celebration" is scheduled for Thursday evening at 6:30 pm local time with approximately 100 guests. The main wedding event is scheduled to run from 5 pm on Friday through 4 am Saturday morning. Street closures around the arena are in effect through Saturday midday, with multiple entrance and drive-through tents being erected around the venue.

The couple has made headlines not only for the wedding itself but also for their charitable giving ahead of the event. Swift and Kelce have donated 26 million dollars to charities across the United States, according to a representative who confirmed the donation to the Guardian. The 20 named charities include organizations in locations meaningful to the couple: Nashville, where Swift began her music career; Kansas City, home of Kelce's NFL team; and New York City, where the wedding is taking place. The recipients include City Harvest and Food Bank for New York City, the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank, and various music education organizations.

Fans have noted that the 26 million dollar figure breaks down to two times Swift's well-known lucky number, 13. The couple's decision to donate before rather than after the wedding aligns with Swift's established practice of giving back. Following her Eras Tour, she gave six-figure bonuses and handwritten letters to her crew members.

A number of high-profile guests have been spotted arriving in New York ahead of the celebrations. Actresses Lena Dunham and Phoebe Waller-Bridge, model Gigi Hadid, musician Ed Sheeran, TV personality Graham Norton, music producer Jack Antonoff, and singer Sabrina Carpenter have all been photographed in formal attire near Madison Square Garden.

Supply deliveries visible around the arena included chicken wings, ground beef, and baked goods from a Brooklyn bakery, suggesting extensive catering preparations for the multi-day event. The permit process for an event of this scale, which requires street closures, can cost as much as 66,000 dollars per day according to the New York Times.

The wedding timing coincides with July Fourth weekend and America's 250th anniversary celebrations. Swift previously described her planned wedding as a large-scale affair when appearing on the Graham Norton show, saying "It's huge" and noting that she would ensure the event remained fun to plan by maintaining an appropriately sized guest list.

cards.headline: Wes Anderson and Bill Murray Discuss Western Film Project
cards.teaser: Director Wes Anderson and actor Bill Murray revealed they have discussed making a Western film together, potentially involving Owen and Luke Wilson.
cards.body:
Wes Anderson and Bill Murray teased a Western project during a surprise onstage reunion in Paris. Anderson said he and Murray have talked for many years about making a Western, potentially with Owen and Luke Wilson involved.

The exchange took place at Cinema Paradiso, a four-day festival of open-air screenings and live music held at the Paris Louvre. The event brought together stars for the surprise announcement about the potential collaboration.

cards.headline: Venice Film Festival Announces Restored Classics Lineup
cards.teaser: The Venice Film Festival will screen 19 restored films including works by Roberto Rossellini, Roger Corman, and Andrej Wajda in its Venice Classics program.
cards.body:
The Venice Film Festival will showcase 19 restored classic films as part of its Venice Classics program. Directors represented include Andrej Wajda, Roberto Rossellini, Luis Buñuel, Roger Corman, John Cassavetes, and Ann Hui.

The lineup features several notable titles, including Wajda's postwar drama Ashes and Diamonds, which Martin Scorsese has cited as one of his ten favorite films. The program also includes Rossellini's Journey to Italy, Corman's The Wild Angels, and Dev Benegal's English, August.

cards.headline: Diego Céspedes Prepares Second Feature Film
cards.teaser: Chilean director Diego Céspedes, who won the top prize at Cannes Un Certain Regard last year, is preparing his second film, The Case of the Boy Who Lost His Heart.
cards.body:
Chilean filmmaker Diego Céspedes is prepping his sophomore film, The Case of the Boy Who Lost His Heart. His debut feature, The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo, won the top prize in Cannes Un Certain Regard last year.

The news comes as another milestone for the 31-year-old director's career. Céspedes emerged as a notable voice in international cinema with his debut feature's success at the French film festival.

cards.headline: Spain and South Africa Launch Audiovisual Venture
cards.teaser: Spanish state investment vehicle SETT and South Africa's Known Associates Group are partnering on a $28.5 million audiovisual venture in Spain.
cards.body:
Spanish state investment vehicle SETT and South Africa's Known Associates Group are partnering on a major audiovisual venture in Spain. The project includes a Madrid-based production company and post-production studios located in the Canary Islands and Basque Country.

SETT, the investment arm of Spain's Ministry for Digital Transformation, is committing $14.5 million to two public-private ventures. The total combined investment in the partnership reaches $28.5 million.

cards.headline: Peter Mullan to Star in Celyn Jones' Film Mountain
cards.teaser: Peter Mullan, Rebecca Lucy Taylor, and Iwan Rheon will lead director Celyn Jones' next feature film, Mountain.
cards.body:
Peter Mullan, Rebecca Lucy Taylor and Iwan Rheon will star in director Celyn Jones' upcoming film Mountain. Jones has previously co-directed The Almond and the Seahorse, which featured Rebel Wilson, and co-wrote The Vanishing with Gerard Butler and Set Fire to the Stars with Elijah Wood.

Mullan recently appeared in I Swear, while Taylor starred in Teeth nSmiles. Rheon is known for his role in Game of Thrones.

cards.headline: Michelle Dockery to Return to Stage After Seven Years
cards.teaser: Downton Abbey star Michelle Dockery will return to theater to lead the world premiere of Bloodsport: After Helen of Troy at Stratford East.
cards.body:
Michelle Dockery will return to the stage for the first time in seven years to lead the world premiere of Ava Pickett's new play, Bloodsport: After Helen of Troy, at Stratford East. Dockery, known for playing Lady Mary Crawley in Downton Abbey, will star as Helen.

Laura Aikman will play Cee opposite Dockery, marking Aikman's stage debut. The production represents a significant return to theater for Dockery after focusing on screen work in recent years.

hero.headline: Democrats prepare subpoenas targeting Trump business dealings
hero.body:
Congressional Democrats are preparing a wave of subpoenas aimed at investigating President Trump's financial activities and those of his associates since winning the 2024 election. The investigation will focus on what Democrats characterize as unprecedented monetization of the presidency, which they estimate has generated billions of dollars in revenue for Trump and his network.

Democrats intend to examine business dealings involving Trump, his family members, close associates, and major donors. The party has framed the investigation as an effort to expose potential conflicts of interest and bring an end to what they view as exploitation of presidential power for financial gain. The White House has denied any conflicts of interest related to the president's business activities.

The investigation mirrors tactics Republicans employed in previous years when they conducted extensive inquiries into the Biden family's business relationships. However, Republicans who control committees in Congress have so far declined to pursue similar investigations into Trump's financial activities, effectively shielding the president from congressional scrutiny by their own party.

The scope of the Democratic investigation appears designed to audit the full range of financial benefits flowing to Trump's orbit since he secured his second term. Party leaders have indicated they view the current situation as unprecedented in the scale of commercial activity connected to a sitting president. The investigation comes as Trump approaches the midpoint of his second year in office.

The preparation of subpoenas represents a significant escalation in Democratic oversight efforts, though the practical impact will depend on which party controls the relevant congressional committees and whether Democrats can compel testimony and document production. The investigation is likely to intensify partisan tensions in Washington as the country marks its 250th anniversary this weekend.

cards.headline: Supreme Court ruling ends transgender rights advocates' hopes for Gorsuch support
cards.teaser: Justice Neil Gorsuch's vote in a recent Supreme Court decision on transgender athlete bans has eliminated expectations he might side with LGBTQ rights advocates.
cards.body:
Transgender rights advocates have abandoned hope that Justice Neil Gorsuch might provide a swing vote on LGBTQ issues before the conservative-majority Supreme Court. That optimism arose from Gorsuch's 2020 decision that employers cannot fire workers based on sexual orientation or gender identity.

Over the past year, Gorsuch has voted against LGBTQ interests in major cases, including a ruling on transgender athletes. The shift has disappointed advocates who believed the Trump appointee might occasionally break with conservative colleagues on questions affecting transgender rights.

cards.headline: Melania Trump pursues policy agenda from White House
cards.teaser: The first lady is working to expand the traditional role of her office to advance specific policy initiatives.
cards.body:
First Lady Melania Trump has developed an active policymaking agenda during her time in the White House, seeking to transform the office beyond its ceremonial functions. She has expressed her intention to place policy proposals before the president for consideration and action.

The first lady's approach represents an effort to evolve the position into one with direct influence on administration priorities. Her office has not specified which policy areas she is targeting or how her initiatives align with broader White House objectives.

cards.headline: GOP lawmakers consider legislation challenging birthright citizenship ruling
cards.teaser: Republican members of Congress are exploring legislative options to counter the Supreme Court's decision upholding birthright citizenship as constitutional.
cards.body:
Republican lawmakers are planning legislation aimed at restricting birthright citizenship following this week's Supreme Court ruling that affirmed it as a constitutional right. Several GOP members have filed or are preparing bills that would target specific practices such as birth tourism or attempt to define who qualifies for citizenship under the jurisdiction clause.

The legislative efforts represent an attempt to work around the court's decision through statutory means. Republicans are exploring whether Congress can impose new limitations on automatic citizenship for children born in the United States without violating the constitutional protections the Supreme Court recognized.

cards.headline: Heat wave forces changes to Washington Fourth of July events
cards.teaser: Organizers of Freedom 250 celebrations in the capital are adjusting plans as temperatures reach triple digits during the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Washington D.C. is facing extreme heat during the country's 250th birthday celebrations this Fourth of July weekend. Temperatures reached 101 degrees on Thursday, with forecasts predicting 103 degrees on Friday, according to the National Weather Service.

The Freedom 250 events, including the Great American State Fair and FIFA Fan Fest, have already drawn 200,000 attendees. Event organizers are implementing heat safety measures as they prepare for larger crowds expected over the holiday weekend amid the significant heat wave gripping the eastern United States.

cards.headline: Democrats balance patriotism with criticism during 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Opposition party leaders are navigating how to challenge President Trump while participating in national celebrations.
cards.body:
Democrats face a strategic challenge during the country's 250th birthday celebrations as President Trump takes center stage at official events. Party leaders are attempting to articulate their own vision of patriotism while criticizing the president's policies and conduct without appearing to reject national unity.

The partisan dynamics surrounding the anniversary have placed Democrats in a position where they must carefully calibrate their messaging. They seek to participate in commemorations while maintaining their opposition to Trump, whose presence dominates the weekend's festivities in Washington.

cards.headline: Political divisions persist as nation marks 250 years
cards.teaser: The country's founding anniversary comes during a period of deep partisan rifts centered on President Trump's polarizing influence.
cards.body:
The United States approaches its 250th anniversary amid deep political divisions, with few expecting the milestone to foster unity. The polarization reflects fundamental disagreements about national identity and values that have intensified in recent years, making unified celebrations increasingly difficult.

The moment carries particular weight for new citizens. Thousands took the naturalization oath as the country neared the anniversary, though some described the experience with unease rather than simple celebration. Meanwhile, faith in the American Dream—a defining ideal since the nation's founding—has been fading among Americans.
